classification.difficultyReason: Compare five vertical translations of an absolute-value graph on shared axes.

content.prompt: On the same set of axes, sketch the graphs of $y=|x|+k$ for $k=-2,-1,0,1,2$.

answer.short: Five upward V-shaped graphs with vertices $(0,-2)$, $(0,-1)$, $(0,0)$, $(0,1)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively.
answer.worked: Translate $y=|x|$ vertically by $k$ units. The graphs retain gradients $-1$ on the left branch and $1$ on the right branch. Their vertices are $(0,k)$: move down 2 units, down 1 unit, leave unchanged, move up 1 unit and move up 2 units, respectively.

spec.sourceRegion: 21D question 4; answer graph at the bottom left of teacher PDF page 34
spec.description: Five vertically translated absolute-value graphs on one coordinate system. Editable series labels identify each value of k; ordinary curves and axes use black.
spec.mathematics: For k=-2,-1,0,1,2, y=|x|+k has vertex (0,k), left gradient -1 and right gradient 1. Drawn segments represent continuing branches.
